name: build_stack_string_and_call
description: Fetches a record through a library call and checks one of its fields. When that field is zero it runs two helpers and conditionally calls library functions on saved handles; otherwise it copies a counted table string and the argument string into a stack buffer, separated by a space, and passes that buffer to a helper. Both paths finish by calling a shared cleanup routine.

name: clean_up_saved_resources_and_reply
description: Runs a helper, then, when the saved result pointer is set, passes up to two saved pointers to library functions. It finishes by calling the exec Forbid and ReplyMsg functions and returns its argument.

name: invoke_two_library_functions
description: Calls two library functions in sequence through fixed negative offsets from the base register, taking no arguments and returning nothing.

name: open_dos_library_or_fail
description: Opens dos.library through the exec base and stores the returned handle in a global; a non-zero result is returned directly. On failure it calls a second library function, runs the shared cleanup and returns a fixed value of 100.

name: parse_command_line_tokens
description: Splits a command string into space-separated tokens, keeping double-quoted text together, and stores each token's start address in a global table; an unterminated quote is reported as an error. With no tokens it opens a console window for input and output; otherwise it obtains the existing input and output handles and opens one more file.

name: allocate_block_with_header
description: Allocates a block 12 bytes larger than the requested size through a library call and stores the address of the usable data area in the block header. It then passes the block to a bookkeeping helper and returns the data-area address, or zero if allocation failed.

name: return_nonzero_or_minus_one
description: Calls a helper with the given argument and returns its result if it is non-zero; otherwise it returns minus one.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one (all bits set) and does nothing else.

name: free_linked_memory_blocks
description: Walks a singly linked list whose head is a global pointer. For each node it calls a library function with the node and the size stored in the node's header, then follows the next pointer until the list ends.

name: append_node_to_list_tail
description: Appends a node to a list whose head and tail pointers are stored in the first structure. The new node's back link takes the old tail, its forward link is cleared, and the head is set only when the list was empty.

name: open_ui_resources_and_init_tables
description: Opens or allocates a series of system resources through library calls, reporting a numbered error for each one that returns zero. It then stores their handles in globals, calls a helper 32 times with zero, and adds 3 to each of 88 entries in a global table.

name: allocate_eight_sized_buffers
description: Allocates eight buffers of fixed sizes through a library call, each with a memory-type flag; when one returns zero it reports error 10 or 11 by number. It then stores one of the buffers in four global slots.

name: load_extra_segment_and_allocate_buffers
description: Allocates an 8000-byte buffer, a 16080-byte buffer and five 2000-byte buffers, reporting an error code for any that fails. It then loads the segment named winter/extra and stores pointers into several globals from the loaded data.

name: read_winter_asset_files
description: Opens files from the winter directory, reads fixed-size blocks into global buffers with seeks between reads, and closes the handles. The referenced names are a paper document file, a felt texture file and a tile file.

name: invoke_title_display_helper
description: Sets a global pointer and calls a helper with the arguments zero, zero, 200, 5, zero and zero. The referenced text names the title file, but the routine itself only makes the call.

name: draw_rectangle_outline
description: Takes four 16-bit coordinates and makes an initial call on a handle with zero, then four successive helper calls that trace the edges of the rectangle they define, returning to the first corner.

name: report_error_message_by_code
description: Looks up a numeric code in a table and jumps to the matching handler. Otherwise it shows the stored error message for the code, from a set covering file-open failures and running out of memory.

name: dispatch_rawkey_message
description: Reads the next message from a port and, when its class is the raw-key input class, looks its key code up in a four-entry table and calls the matching handler, returning that result. Other messages return the message pointer.

name: point_inside_rectangle
description: Returns one if the point given by the first two arguments lies inside the rectangle described by four words in the third argument, edges included, and zero otherwise.

name: poll_message_for_key_flag
description: Fetches the next message from a port and copies it into a 60-byte stack buffer. It returns zero for a raw-key message with one specific key code and one otherwise, changing the message's state field for one other message class. It returns one when no message is pending.

name: wait_for_nonzero_result_then_process
description: Calls two setup helpers and two library functions, then loops calling a helper until it returns a non-zero value and passes that value to another helper. It then calls a helper with four stored parameters and a stored value, and stores a fixed constant in a global.

name: read_header_and_fill_entries
description: Opens a file, reads a 64-byte header into a stack buffer and calls a helper once for each entry in a count. Each call uses an offset built from the entry index and a 40-byte stride. It closes the file and passes the header with a bit mask to a further helper.

name: unpack_word_fields_into_calls
description: Walks a table of 16-bit words between two indices and, for each word, calls a helper with the running index, the high byte, the middle nibble and the low nibble.

name: call_helper_for_32_indices
description: Calls a helper 32 times, passing each index from zero to 31 together with zero for the remaining arguments.

name: pass_stored_handle_to_helper
description: Passes a stored global handle to one helper call and returns. It has no other effect.

name: pass_stored_handle_to_library
description: Passes a stored global handle to one helper, which calls the library function at offset minus 54, and returns.

name: apply_display_state_record
description: Looks up a 16-byte record by index and passes its words and a stored handle to a helper. For index 2 it sets a field of the handle to a stored value and calls a helper with a second stored value; for index 3 it clears that field and calls the helper with zero.

name: forbid_multitasking_stub
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 132 of a stored base, the usual exec Forbid entry, and returns.

name: allocate_memory_stub
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 198 of a stored base, the usual exec AllocMem entry, and returns.

name: format_text_into_bounded_buffer
description: Expands a printf-style format string into a destination buffer, copying literal characters and turning a doubled percent sign into one percent sign. Each conversion is expanded by a helper into a 256-byte temporary and copied in; characters that do not fit are passed one at a time to an output helper, and an end marker is sent at the close.

name: open_timer_device_request
description: Creates a message port and a 40-byte I/O request, then opens timer.device with the request. Failures are reported with numbered error codes, and the request is returned on success.

name: start_timer_request
description: Sets the command field of a timer request to 9, stores the supplied time value, clears another field, and sends the request asynchronously through the device library call.

name: release_io_request_chain
description: Releases an I/O request together with the request linked from one of its fields, calling helpers on each and closing the device through a library call. A null pointer is ignored.

name: release_stored_requests_in_order
description: Calls a helper on the second stored request, then on the first, then on the second again, taking no arguments.

name: open_input_device_request
description: Creates a message port and an I/O request, then opens input.device with it. On an open failure it releases the port and request, reports a numbered error and returns.

name: prepare_input_handler_request
description: Calls two helpers on stored handles with the value 256, clears a local record, and sets a request's command to 11 with its data pointing at that record. It sends the request and then issues two more helper calls on stored handles.

name: send_clamped_input_command
description: Passes a stored value, selected by the argument, to a helper together with a stored handle. When a stored flag is set, it sends a request with command 14 whose data is the argument, reset to zero unless it is 0 or 1.

name: compute_single_bit_mask_and_apply
description: Builds a single-bit value from a byte field of a stored structure and passes it to a helper that returns a result. That result and a stored field of the structure are then passed to a second helper.

name: load_pix_and_animate_sprites
description: Opens and reads the picture files winter/pix1 and winter/pix2 into buffers, then runs a sprite loop that blits pieces from position tables and waits on a timing counter. The listing is cut off part-way through the animation loop, so its later steps are not visible.

name: blit_scene_pieces
description: Computes two scaled coordinates from stored values and issues many helper calls that copy rectangles at fixed positions and sizes, with extra pieces when a stored flag is clear. It then waits until a stored counter reaches 160 and copies one more piece.

name: call_helper_n_times
description: Calls a helper once for each step of a counter up to the argument's value, taking no arguments itself.

name: fill_global_table_entries
description: Makes twenty calls to a helper, passing the global table entry at the index each call returns. It then calls a helper with an incrementing index up to a stored count, and finally calls a helper with its two arguments.

name: build_grouped_item_records
description: Fills consecutive 34-byte records for each of four groups, using per-group counts from globals. Each record gets a position, a size and a pointer into a global area, and several flag words and marker bytes are set. It finishes by polling a helper until it returns a non-zero value.

name: poll_helper_until_nonzero
description: Calls a helper with its argument and a global address repeatedly until it returns a non-zero value.

name: mark_list_entry_text
description: Walks a linked list from a record's head pointer to the node at the given position, then writes a space or an asterisk, chosen by the flag argument, into the text buffer that node points to. Nothing happens when the position is past the end.

name: copy_bytes_forward
description: Copies a counted number of bytes from a source to a destination one at a time, moving forwards.

name: store_long_through_pointer_field
description: Stores the second argument as a 32-bit value in a field of the structure reached through a pointer held in the first argument.

name: call_library_entry_30
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 30 of a stored base and returns.

name: call_library_entry_54
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 54 of a stored base and returns.

name: call_library_entry_66
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 66 of a stored base and returns.

name: call_library_entry_72
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 72 of a stored base and returns. One routine calls this stub.

name: wait_for_blitter
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 228 of a stored base, the graphics blitter wait entry, and returns. It does nothing else, and two routines call it.

name: call_library_entry_240
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 240 of a stored base and returns. Eleven routines call this stub.

name: call_library_entry_246
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 246 of a stored base and returns. Eight routines call this stub.

name: call_library_entry_252
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 252 of a stored base and returns. One routine calls this stub.

name: call_library_entry_264
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 264 of a stored base and returns. One routine calls this stub.

name: call_library_entry_270
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 270 of a stored base and returns. Six routines call this stub.

name: call_library_entry_282
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 282 of a stored base and returns. One routine calls this stub.

name: call_library_entry_354
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 354 of a stored base and returns. Seven routines call this stub.

name: allocate_five_buffers_and_swap_field
description: Allocates five buffers of fixed sizes through library calls with memory-type flags, reporting error 103 for any that fail. It then reads a field of the current task, saves it in a global and replaces it with a stored value.

name: run_mode_four_request_and_return
description: Calls a helper with mode four and two stored arguments and subtracts one from its result. When that is zero it calls a second helper and returns that value; otherwise it returns the decremented result.

name: load_numbered_resource
description: Calls a helper with the stored arguments, the fixed code 1830 and mode one, and passes any non-zero result to another helper.

name: run_mode_five_request_and_return
description: Calls a helper with mode five and two stored arguments and subtracts one from its result. When that is zero it calls a second helper and returns that value; otherwise it returns the decremented result.

name: run_selector_input_loop
description: Copies two stored strings into local buffers, sets up the item list, then loops on a helper that returns an input code. Codes 12 and 13 move the highlighted position up and down within bounds, and the other codes are handled by helpers. The loop exits on codes 1, 2 or 14, copies the buffers back out and returns the code.

name: run_selector_loop_stack_frame
description: Runs the same selector input loop as the neighbouring routine, but it takes its buffers from the caller's stack frame rather than from parameters. It returns the final input code.

name: resume_selector_input_loop
description: Continues the selector input loop from the point where the item list is refilled, without setup. It exits through the same copy-out and return steps as the selector loop.

name: refill_selector_items_and_loop
description: Refills the six visible item entries from the stored list, starting at a stored offset, then runs the selector input loop, calling helpers that handle the list and selection. It returns the final input code.

name: draw_selector_frame
description: Calculates a rectangle from stored position and size fields, expanded by a few units on each side, and passes it with a fixed value to a helper.

name: draw_highlight_box_around_item
description: When a stored entry has a child structure, fills the entry's rectangle through a helper and then draws lines around its edges using the entry's coordinates. It uses the same edge-tracing pattern as the rectangle outline routine.

name: refresh_selector_display
description: Runs three helper calls, then passes the child structure of a stored entry, when present, with a stored value to a helper. It finishes with one helper call on a second stored value.

name: bracket_helper_call_with_handle
description: Calls a helper on a stored handle with zero, then calls the argument's helper, then calls the stored handle again with minus one. It returns the helper's result.

name: pass_stored_pair_to_helper
description: Passes two stored values and a global address to a helper and returns.

name: scan_directory_entries_into_list
description: Skips leading spaces in a name argument, then locks the named path through a helper and reads its entries into a list. The list holds up to 78 names, each cut to 22 characters, and the routine returns a code that shows whether the scan completed.

name: lock_directory_and_scan_entries
description: Locks the directory named in the frame for reading, and if that fails it reports the system error code and returns one. Otherwise it examines the directory, sets a flag when its type field equals a fixed value, and runs the entry loop. It returns zero, two or three depending on the outcome.

name: examine_directory_and_scan
description: Examines a locked directory, records a flag when its type field equals a fixed value, and runs the entry loop. It returns two when the type field is negative and otherwise returns zero or three.

name: start_directory_entry_loop
description: Clears a flag and returns two when the stored entry has a negative type field. Otherwise it runs the entry loop, releases the directory and returns three.

name: loop_over_directory_entries
description: Reads directory entries one at a time, passing each to a helper and copying the names of matching entries into the list, cut to 22 characters, until the list reaches 78 entries or the scan ends. It returns zero when a stored code equals 232, otherwise it releases the directory and returns three.

name: repeat_directory_scan_passes
description: Repeats scan passes: each pass clears a stored count, calls two helpers and runs the entry loop. It returns zero when a stored code equals 232, and otherwise releases the directory and returns three.

name: collect_entries_in_repeating_passes
description: Runs the entry collection loop in repeating passes without clearing the stored count first. It returns zero when a stored code equals 232, and otherwise releases the directory and returns three.

name: unlock_directory_and_return_three
description: Unlocks the stored directory lock through a library call, makes a second helper call with the value two, and returns three.

name: restore_saved_structure_field
description: Writes a value saved in a global back into a field of a stored structure. This reverses the field replacement made by the buffer allocation routine.

name: resolve_named_path_and_run
description: Takes a name argument, removes leading spaces, and appends a separator when the name does not end in a colon or slash. It locks the path to check that it exists, then calls a helper with the name and a 100-byte buffer, restores the saved state and the current-directory lock, and returns the helper's result.

name: transfer_file_with_size_check
description: Opens a named file for reading (mode zero) or writing (mode one), transfers its data, and compares the byte counts with the expected total. It returns 100 on the first failure path and zero when the sizes match; any other mismatch returns the stored error code.

name: load_numbered_resource_from_dir
description: Calls the current-directory helper, then calls a helper with the stored argument, the fixed code 1830 and the second argument. A non-zero result sets mode one and is passed to a further helper.

name: verify_sum_after_numbered_load
description: Sums a list of stored values, performs a numbered load, and sums the list again when the load returns a non-zero result. A helper is called when the two sums differ.

name: verify_frame_sum_after_load
description: Performs a numbered load and, when it succeeds, sums a list of stored values into a frame slot and compares it with a second frame slot. A helper is called when the sums differ.

name: check_frame_sum_mismatch
description: Compares two stored frame values and calls a helper when they differ, then calls another helper.

name: configure_option_display_state
description: Sets up the option display from several stored settings. It calls helpers chosen by whether each setting is zero, applies a fixed set of values for the chosen mode and refreshes four entries in a loop. A stored value of 144 selects one final helper call instead.

name: dispatch_large_key_record
description: Searches a table of three-word records for a key and, when the key is above 99 and a record is found, calls a helper with that record's second word. The table is not changed.

name: dispatch_found_key_record
description: Searches the same table of three-word records for a key and calls a helper with the second word of the matching record. Nothing happens when no record matches.

name: call_helper_if_index_within_limit
description: Calls a helper with a word read from a stored pointer, but only when the frame's counter is within the limit held in the frame.

name: find_name_in_entry_list
description: Searches a list of 32-byte entries for one equal to the given name, comparing character by character after converting each character to upper case. Returns one on a match and zero otherwise.

name: compare_first_chars_in_entries
description: Walks the same 32-byte entry list, comparing the first character of the frame's name with the first character of each entry, and sets a found flag when they match.

name: return_frame_found_flag
description: Returns the found flag held in the caller's stack frame.

name: convert_char_to_uppercase
description: Returns the byte at the given address converted to upper case when it is a lower-case letter, by clearing the bit that separates the two cases.

name: read_volume_info_for_total
description: Locks the volume named by the device text, reads its information block into a 36-byte buffer, and adds a value derived from the block's status field to a stored total. Nothing is added when the lock or the information read fails.

name: call_library_entry_42
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 42 of a stored base and returns.

name: call_library_entry_150
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 150 of a stored base and returns.

name: set_up_audio_device_requests
description: Allocates a 1496-byte block and a message port, then fills 22 request records, setting a volume byte of 127 and an index byte in each. It opens audio.device with the first request, reporting error code 400 or 401 on failure, and then calls a helper for each of ten entries, storing and shifting the results that succeed.

name: release_audio_request_blocks
description: Returns at once when a stored flag is set. Otherwise it makes two release helper calls on stored blocks, then releases each non-zero entry in the ten-slot table.

name: release_audio_segment_and_blocks
description: Calls a helper, releases two stored blocks, then releases each non-zero entry in the ten-slot table.

name: queue_audio_channel_requests
description: Returns at once when a stored flag is set. Otherwise it clamps its argument to the range 0 to 3, frees the in-use slots recorded in a bit mask, and fills up to 20 free request slots over two passes with pointers, lengths and fixed values before queuing each one.

name: queue_audio_table_entries
description: Returns at once when a stored flag is set. Otherwise it clears finished slots from the in-use bit mask, then fills free request slots from the four-word table entries for the given index and queues each one.

name: stop_audio_and_drain_requests
description: Sets fixed values in a control request and sends it, then clears the in-use bits of finished requests. It sends one request for each remaining bit until none are left.

name: drain_audio_request_mask
description: While the in-use mask is non-zero, it clears the bits of finished requests and sends a request for each remaining bit.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: create_message_port
description: Allocates a signal bit and a 34-byte port block, then stores the given value and the current task pointer in it. It either initialises a list inside the port or adds the port to a list, and returns the block, or zero if allocation fails.

name: delete_message_port
description: Removes the port from its list when a link field is set, marks its status fields as deleted, frees its signal bit and releases its memory block.

name: empty_stub_function
description: Does nothing and returns; the decompiled body has no effect on memory or I/O.

name: wait_and_dispatch_port_messages
description: Loops waiting for messages on a port while handling pending events through a helper. Messages of one class are skipped; the others are copied into a local buffer, released, and matched against a four-entry table of codes, with the matching handler called when found.

name: match_code_sequence_and_dispatch
description: Compares a message field with the next entry of a short code table and advances a stored sequence index on a match. The index is reset when the field lacks a flag bit. It then waits for a port message, skipping messages of one class, and dispatches the rest through a four-entry table.

name: repeat_code_sequence_and_dispatch
description: Repeats the same code sequence check and port message wait as the previous routine, dispatching through the same four-entry table.

name: reset_code_sequence_and_dispatch
description: Resets the stored sequence index when a flag bit in the message is clear, then waits for a port message and dispatches it through the four-entry table, as its neighbours do.

name: build_path_from_entry_list
description: Walks a list of directory entries, saving up to ten entry pointers, and copies their names into a path string in reverse order with separators between them. A non-zero argument only calls one helper and returns.

name: call_helper_once
description: Calls one helper with no arguments and returns.

name: copy_string_to_offset
description: Calls a helper with the first argument to get an offset, then copies the null-terminated string at the second argument into the buffer at that offset. It returns the first argument.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Calls a helper for an offset, then copies the string at the second argument into the buffer, stopping at a null byte or after the length given as the third argument. It always writes a terminating null and returns the first argument.

name: expand_format_string
description: Copies a format string into an output area through a pointer kept in a structure, turning a doubled percent sign into one percent sign and expanding conversions through a helper. When the output count is exhausted each byte is passed to an output helper, and an end marker is sent at the close.

name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Sets the first word of a block to point four bytes past the block's own start, clears the second word, and stores the block's address in the third word, forming an empty self-linked list header.

name: count_string_bytes
description: Counts the bytes from a given address up to, but not including, the first zero byte, and returns that count.

name: read_next_stream_byte
description: Returns the next byte of a buffered stream, calling a refill helper when its count is exhausted. It returns all ones when the stream's state flags show an error or end condition.

name: read_next_stream_byte_from_frame
description: Reads the next byte of the buffered stream held in the caller's frame, refilling its buffer through a helper when the count runs out. It returns all ones when the stream is in an error or end state.

name: refill_stream_buffer_and_read
description: Refills a stream's buffer through a helper using its block size, sets end-of-data or error flags from the count returned, and then returns the next byte. It returns all ones when the stream is already in a non-readable state.

name: start_stream_buffer_fill
description: Marks the stream as being read, fills its buffer through a helper, and sets end-of-data or error flags from the result. It then returns the next byte.

name: fill_stream_buffer_and_return_byte
description: Marks the stream as being read, fills its buffer through a helper with the stored block size, sets end or error flags from the result, and returns the next byte.

name: read_next_buffered_byte
description: Returns the next byte from the buffer held in a stream structure. When the remaining count is exhausted it calls a refill helper first.

name: pass_frame_stream_to_helper
description: Passes the stream pointer held in the caller's frame to one helper call and returns.

name: write_byte_with_retry
description: Writes one byte into a buffer structure, advancing its pointer and count. When the count underflows it calls a flush helper, and it records errors reported by that helper as flag bits in the state byte. Returns the byte written, or all ones when the stream is in an error or end state.

name: allocate_stream_buffer
description: Returns zero when a buffer is already set and the reset flag is clear. Otherwise it obtains a new buffer through a helper, stores it in the structure's first and fourth words, and clears its flags and counters. On failure it stores error code 12 and returns minus one.

name: parse_option_letter_and_dispatch
description: Skips an optional minus sign, spaces, a period and a letter l, then looks the next character up in a table of nine entries and calls the matching handler. Returns zero when no entry matches.

name: format_float_with_precision
description: Sets the precision from the frame, defaulting to six and capped at nineteen, then calls a conversion helper and writes the sign, digits, decimal point and exponent into the output buffer. The listing is cut off part-way through the exponent branch, so its later steps are not visible.

name: format_float_alternate_entry
description: Alternate entry into the number formatting routine: it sets the mode flag to one and then runs the same conversion and output steps as the routine above. The listing is cut off part-way through.

name: continue_float_formatting
description: Runs the number formatting steps from the point after the mode flag is set, converting the value and writing its digits, decimal point and exponent to the output buffer. The listing is cut off part-way through.

name: pad_output_buffer_and_return
description: Writes a fill byte into the output buffer for each remaining count, stores the new buffer position through a pointer, and returns the stored count plus one.

name: copy_digits_and_pad_output
description: Writes a fill byte for the remaining padding count, then copies a run of digits from the source pointer into the output buffer. It stores the new position through a pointer and returns the stored count plus one.

name: copy_digit_run_to_output
description: Copies a counted run of digits from the source pointer into the output buffer, stores the new position through a pointer, and returns the stored count plus one.

name: copy_value_and_increment_counter
description: Stores a value from the frame through a pointer held in the frame and returns another frame field plus one.

name: format_float_mid_entry
description: Runs the number formatting steps from the point where the conversion helper is called, with no setup. The listing is cut off part-way through the exponent branch.

name: format_float_from_saved_value
description: Converts the value saved in the frame with the conversion helper and writes its sign, digits, decimal point and exponent into the output buffer, using the same steps as the neighbouring formatter entries. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: write_point_digits_and_exponent
description: Writes zero padding, a decimal point and a run of digits into the output buffer, then writes the exponent letter, its sign and its digits. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: compute_width_and_write_fraction
description: Derives a width from the magnitude of the stored value, adding digits above 99 and above 999, then writes fill characters, a sign and the fraction digits. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: write_zero_fraction_digits
description: Writes a decimal point and zero fraction digits into the output buffer, using the remaining fraction count held in the frame.

name: write_sign_and_fraction_digits
description: Writes a minus sign when one is needed, then the integer digits from the source, a decimal point and the fraction digits. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: write_zeros_then_pad_output
description: Writes zero digits, then fill characters while a counter remains, stores the new output position and returns it plus one.

name: write_zero_digits_and_pad
description: Writes zero digits and copies the remaining digits from the source pointer. When a flag is set it pads the output with fill characters, then returns the output position plus one.

name: write_digits_with_decimal_point
description: Copies the remaining integer digits from the source, writes a decimal point while fraction digits remain, writes those digits and pads the output. It returns the output position plus one.

name: write_zero_point_digits_and_pad
description: Writes zero digits, then a decimal point and fraction digits while the fraction count is non-zero, and fill characters when a flag is set. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: finish_decimal_digits_and_return
description: Writes a decimal point while fraction digits remain, writes the remaining digits and fill characters, stores the output position and returns the count plus one.

name: write_zero_digits_and_return
description: Writes zero digits and a fill run, stores the output position through a pointer and returns the count plus one.

name: write_exponent_letter_and_sign
description: Writes a decimal point and digits, then the exponent letter and its sign. The listing is cut off part-way through the exponent digits.

name: write_zero_point_exponent
description: Writes a zero digit and a decimal point, then the exponent digits and sign. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: write_exponent_loop_digits
description: Writes a zero digit, then the exponent letter and sign, and the exponent digits in a loop until the count is used up.

name: write_exponent_digits_and_pad
description: Writes the exponent letter and sign, then the exponent digits from a digit table, padding with fill characters when a flag is set. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: write_plus_sign_and_exponent_digits
description: Writes a plus sign, then the exponent digits from the digit table into the output buffer, followed by a padding copy when a flag is set. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: copy_fill_run_and_return
description: Copies a run of fill characters into the output buffer, stores the new position through a pointer and returns the stored count plus one.

name: copy_value_and_increment_counter
description: Stores a value from the frame through a pointer held in the frame and returns another frame field plus one.

name: create_io_request
description: Allocates a memory block for an I/O request when the first argument is non-zero, sets its type byte to 5, and stores the size and the port pointer in it. Returns the block, or zero if allocation fails.

name: delete_io_request
description: Marks an I/O request as deleted by setting its status and two result fields, then frees its memory block using the size stored in it. Does nothing for a null pointer.

name: create_standard_io_request
description: Creates an I/O request of a fixed 48-byte size by passing that size to the request creation routine.

name: delete_standard_io_request
description: Passes its pointer argument unchanged to the request deletion routine and returns.

name: combine_helper_outputs_scaled
description: Calls a helper that fills two local words, then returns the first word times 256 plus the second word shifted right by 12 bits.

name: pad_negative_entry_text
description: Fills in a list entry from a global area and stores a computed width in each entry of a linked list. Negative text entries are padded with minus signs to that width. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: draw_offset_marker_pair
description: Computes two offset coordinates from stored values and makes two helper calls with them, one for the first point and one for the second.

name: draw_two_fixed_size_blits
description: Reads position values from helpers and issues two blit-style helper calls with a fixed size of 20 by 23 and a mask setting, the second with a different mode, drawing two panel images at the given coordinates.

name: draw_four_offset_points
description: Makes one helper call with the value 15, then four helper calls at the given position and at offsets of 19 across and 22 down, combining the two offsets in each pairing.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: clear_entry_status_bit
description: Finds an entry through a helper and clears bit four of its status word.

name: clear_entry_status_mask
description: Finds an entry through a helper, clears the bits given by the mask argument in its status word, and calls a helper on a stored handle before and after that change.

name: get_list_item_by_index
description: Walks forward from the list head stored in the structure, stepping the number of times given by the argument. Returns the node reached, or zero if the list ends first.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: store_four_words
description: Stores four 16-bit arguments into consecutive words at the given pointer.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: advance_random_lfsr
description: Advances a 32-bit linear feedback shift register held in a global by one step, applying a fixed feedback constant when the top bit was set, and returns its low 16 bits.

name: count_list_nodes
description: Counts the nodes of the linked list whose head pointer is stored in the structure and returns the count.

name: draw_entry_at_position
description: When the entry's top flag bit is clear, draws it at its stored position through two helper calls and then calls a helper on the entry. When the flag is set it only calls that final helper.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: draw_two_fixed_boxes
description: Makes two rectangle helper calls with fixed coordinates and sizes, each followed by a helper call on the global handle.

name: set_entry_highlight_state
description: Sets or clears the top flag bit of an entry, calling a helper on the global handle when the bit changes. It stores 31 or 6 in one state byte of the entry depending on whether the argument is zero, then calls a helper on the entry.

name: draw_three_fixed_boxes
description: Makes three rectangle helper calls with fixed coordinates and sizes, each followed by a helper call on the global handle.

name: draw_text_string_at_entry
description: Sets three state values through helper calls, measures the length of the null-terminated string argument, and passes the string and its length to a text drawing helper.

name: draw_text_with_state_value
description: Like the neighbouring text routine, but it uses the second argument as one of its state values, then measures the string and passes it to the text drawing helper.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: forward_two_words_to_helper
description: Passes its two 16-bit arguments, together with a stored handle, to one helper call and returns.

name: copy_eight_bytes_to_stack
description: Copies eight bytes from the source pointer into a local stack buffer, one byte at a time.

name: clip_sprite_to_neighbours
description: Computes overlap extents of a sprite against neighbouring table entries and adjusts its drawn rectangle, then calls a helper. The listing is cut off part-way through the clipping logic.

name: hit_test_with_neighbour_bounds
description: Returns one when a point lies inside a rectangle whose bounds are adjusted from neighbouring table entries, applying a special case when the entry index is 88. The listing is cut off after the first check.

name: compute_neighbour_overlap_extents
description: Computes overlap extents of an entry against its neighbours from a global position table, clamping negative extents to zero. It is the first part of a hit test, and the listing is cut off before the test completes.

name: check_entry_88_hit_region
description: Computes one neighbour overlap extent with clamping. When the entry index is 88 it returns one if the point lies inside the entry's rectangle. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: test_point_in_extent_rect_hit
description: Tests whether a point lies inside an entry's rectangle adjusted by the computed extents. Entry 88 uses its plain bounds, while other entries use bounds shrunk by the extents on each side. Returns one on a hit, and the listing is cut off part-way.

name: test_point_in_extent_rect_alt
description: Continues the point hit test with the other extent combinations and returns one on any hit. The listing is cut off part-way.

name: test_point_in_bottom_extent_rect
description: Returns one when a point lies inside the entry's rectangle, bounded by the top and bottom extents, and zero otherwise.

name: test_point_in_left_extent_rect
description: Returns one when a point lies inside the entry's rectangle, bounded by the left and right extents, and zero otherwise.

name: return_zero
description: Returns zero.

name: lookup_grid_neighbour
description: Looks up a value from a 15-column grid of 120 cells stored as a table. It computes a column and row from the given offsets and returns zero when either falls outside the grid, otherwise the table entry at the computed index.

name: return_without_effect
description: Does nothing and returns to its caller.

name: mark_entry_and_draw_frame
description: Calls a helper on the global handle with the entry, sets the entry's top flag bit, computes a rectangle a few units larger than the entry, and draws it through a helper call.

name: forward_entry_position_to_helper
description: Passes the first two fields of the entry, together with its argument, to one helper call and returns.

name: call_helper_with_zero
description: Calls one helper with the argument zero and returns.

name: advance_entry_counters_and_call
description: Increments two 16-bit counter fields of the entry and passes the entry with the argument to one helper call.

name: draw_alternating_border_frames
description: Draws a bordered shape in a loop over a count taken from a global, alternating between two values for each step and drawing each edge with a line helper. The listing is cut off part-way.
